questions.q: Select the correct indirect speech: He said, “Let us wait for the doctor.”
opts: He told to wait for the doctor.
He suggested that let them wait for the doctor.
He suggested that they should wait for the doctor.
He said that let us wait for the doctor.
questions.why: 'Let us' becomes 'suggested/proposed that they should'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct version: “He is the man whom I think is responsible for the leak.”
opts: He is the man whom I think he is responsible for the leak.
He is the man who I think he is responsible for the leak.
He is the man who I think is responsible for the leak.
He is the man who I think are responsible for the leak.
questions.why: 'Who' is the subject of 'is responsible'; 'I think' is parenthetical. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct form: “She is one of those nurses who ____ always punctual.”
questions.why: 'Who' refers to the plural 'nurses', so the verb is plural. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct inversion of: “If he were to apologise, I would forgive him.”
opts: Be he to apologise, I would forgive him.
Were he to apologise, I would forgive him.
Did he to apologise, I would forgive him.
Should he were to apologise, I would forgive him.
questions.why: 'If ... were to' is inverted as 'Were + subject + to'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct form: “Not only the students but also the teacher ____ responsible.”
questions.why: The verb agrees with the nearer subject 'the teacher'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Select the correct indirect speech: He will say, “I am busy.”
opts: He will say that he was busy.
He will say that he had been busy.
He will say that he is busy.
He will say that he would be busy.
questions.why: When the reporting verb is in the future tense, there is no backshift. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “extol”:
questions.why: To extol is to praise highly; to denigrate is to belittle. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive construction: “Do not touch the wires.”
opts: Let not the wires be touched.
The wires are not to touch.
Let not the wires being touched.
questions.why: Negative imperative passive: Let not + object + be + past participle. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct form: “I remember ____ the letter yesterday; I posted it myself.”
questions.why: 'Remember' + gerund refers to a past act recalled. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct tense: “When we reached the cinema, the film ____ for ten minutes.”
questions.why: Duration up to a past moment takes the past perfect continuous. GPSC-style practice item.
